subject: Renewal readiness: traffic to commit & ROI summary
messages:
From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@zephyr.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@zephyr.ai
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal review: usage signals & Q1 commit

Hi Marissa,

Quick note ahead of next week's sync — wanted to share our October usage and a couple of questions that will feed into procurement. Attached is the raw export (zephyr_oct_usage_report.csv). High-level:
- Average tokens/day up ~45% MoM driven by search + summarization workloads.
- Spiky peak periods around product launches (see 10/19 and 10/27).
- We still see occasional 95th pct latency spikes on long-chat sessions.

Questions for you:
1) Is there a recommended commit path that buys headroom for burst events but keeps unit costs sensible?
2) Can you share the ROI recap you mentioned earlier (token efficiency changes and expected cost per 1M tokens after proposed quantization)?

If it helps, happy to share a short sample of payloads for the SREs.

Thanks — looking to get an early read for procurement next week.

Tom
Tom Chen
Head of Product
ZephyrAI

Attachments: zephyr_oct_usage_report.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Chen <tom.chen@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review: usage signals & Q1 commit

On Mon, Nov 1, 2026 at 09:12 AM Tom Chen <tom.chen@zephyr.ai> wrote:
> Quick note ahead of next week's sync — wanted to share our October usage and a couple of questions that will feed into procurement.

Thanks Tom — this is helpful. We reviewed the CSV and ran a quick token-efficiency projection. A few quick takeaways:
- Headroom model: recommend a stepped commit with two components — a baseline monthly commit sized at ~1.25x your 90-day run-rate, plus a burst credit pool you can draw from during launches. That buys predictable unit pricing on steady traffic and keeps costs bounded for spikes.
- Unit economics: with the quantization profile we discussed (int8 + selective KV caching), expected blended cost per 1M tokens drops ~27% vs today. I'll attach a short latency sample and the ROI slide.
- Latency spikes: ops note — most of the 95th pct spikes correlate with >4k prompt lengths plus concurrent reranking jobs. Monica, can your ops team confirm whether we can shift reranking to off-peak or move to a dedicated pool for those windows?

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to confirm feasibility of rerank scheduling + an ops runbook for bursts.
2) Karthik to produce a commit proposal with pricing tiers + example cost for baseline + 100% burst usage.
3) I will draft a short amendment (term + burst credit language) and a one-page ROI recap for procurement.

I'll include a sample amendment and the latency file in the next message.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency_sample_10k.json (sample logs), proposed_amendment_v2.docx
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: ops feasibility for Zephyr rerank windows

Marissa/Karthik — quick ops check after looking into Tom's CSV:
- Rerank jobs are currently colocated on shared pools. We can move Zephyr's scheduled reranks to a nightly dedicated slot that would cut the observed 95th pct spikes by ~60% (rough estimate).
- Dedicated pool increases cost but can be offset if Zephyr takes a committed burst pool; ops can tag those jobs for preferential scheduling when burst credits are available.
- I recommend adding a short SLA clause for queueing/priority during launches and a playbook for enabling burst credits.

I'll prepare a short runbook and a rough delta for ops cost by EOD tomorrow.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal review: usage signals & Q1 commit

Marissa — I ran numbers on three commit scenarios (baseline, baseline+burst pool, and runway-accelerator).
Tom — happy to present these in your procurement call; short summary:
- Baseline (1.25x 90-day run-rate): lowest immediate spend, limited burst protection.
- Baseline + burst pool (recommended): moderate commit with 30% discount on baseline tokens and tiered pricing for burst consumption; best balance for launches.
- Runway-accelerator (higher commit): material unit discounts but requires longer term.

I'll attach the spreadsheet into HubSpot and can join procurement next week.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Pricing: baseline tokens at 30% discount vs list; burst consumed from pooled credits at a tiered rate (see attached proposed_amendment_v2.docx).
- Ops: Monica to deliver runbook + scheduled rerank slot; expected latency improvement of ~60% at p95.
- Legal/Procurement: We will provide a one-page ROI recap and proposed amendment. DocuSign link below for the amendment once procurement signoff is complete.
